rics.meaning: Average Monthly Wages — average net wage of formal-sector employees, published by BPS in the Sakernas (National Labor Force Survey).
rics.how_to_use: Indonesia minimum wages are set provincially (UMP) and revised annually. Average monthly wages run well above minimum (urban formal sector ~Rp 3-4 million; minimum wage range Rp 2-5 million by province). Watch annual UMP decisions in late-Q4 for next year's labor-cost trajectory.

rics.description: Average Monthly Wages, Average, Chg Y/Y
rics.meaning: Average Monthly Wages, year-over-year change — wage growth rate.
rics.how_to_use: Indonesia wage growth typically runs 5-8% YoY (well above CPI inflation 2-3%, real wage growth ~3-5%). Sharp acceleration signals minimum-wage hikes; deceleration signals labor-market slack.

rics.meaning: Monthly Average Wage — Manufacturing — average wage in the manufacturing sector specifically.
rics.how_to_use: Track manufacturing wages for unit-labor-cost trends. Indonesia competes with Vietnam, Bangladesh, India on labor-cost competitiveness in light manufacturing — sustained wage growth above productivity growth signals erosion.
